{"data":{"id":"478007361549","type":"page","title":"Runbook: Tailored Brands","status":"current","spaceId":"4708335613","snapshotToken":"v:2","detail":"full","body":{"format":"markdown","value":"# Runbook: Tailored Brands

**Volume rank:** #6 (15 incidents / trailing 180 days)  
**Primary products:** Secure Incident, Secure (transaction data), Power BI reporting  
**Abbrev:** TBI

## Recurring themes

| Theme | Signal | Typical tickets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missing / incomplete transaction data | Expected transactions absent or partial | RCS-27283 (value too long for varchar(100)) |
| Secure Incident access | User unable to access Secure Incident | RCS-27578 |
| Secure Incident field / print issues | Fields blank on printer-friendly report; required fields empty on closed incidents | RCS-27643, RCS-27459 |
| SmartLink not generating | Custom Fit Order SmartLink returns no results | RCS-27461 |
| Report / query timeouts | Power BI export / query slow or failing | RCS-27392 |

## Diagnostic playbook

**Missing / incomplete transaction data**

1. Identify store, date, and the specific transactions expected vs. present.
2. Note the recurring "value too long for varchar(100)" load failure: a source field exceeding the column length will reject rows at load. Check load logs for truncation/reject errors.
3. If a field-length reject is found, coordinate a schema/mapping fix with DataOps/Engineering.

**Secure Incident access**

1. Confirm single user vs. broader; compare role/access level against a working peer.
2. Restore at role level if config; escalate if the app rejects a valid user.

**Secure Incident field / print issues**

1. Reproduce on the named report (e.g. Associate Reported field blank on PrinterFriendlyReport).
2. Determine whether the field is empty in the data or dropped only in the print/render layer.
3. "Incidents showing closed with required fields empty" suggests a workflow/validation defect: escalate to Engineering.

**SmartLink not generating**

1. Get the exact order number (e.g. Custom Order 7760761) and the SmartLink used.
2. Confirm whether matching source records exist for that order before treating as a defect.

## Escalation routing

- Load / field-length rejects: DataOps + Engineering.
- Access/config: self-resolve or Onboarding.
- Field/render/workflow defect: Engineering (escalation brief).
- Reporting/Power BI performance: Performance review.

## Reference tickets

RCS-27643, RCS-27578, RCS-27461, RCS-27459, RCS-27392, RCS-27283

## Key contacts / notes

*Fill in verified client and Appriss contacts here. Do not assume org affiliation.*

{"data":{"id":"477497557009","type":"page","title":"Tailored Brands Gateway Pull Support Guide and Troubleshooting Workflow","status":"current","spaceId":"474882342984","snapshotToken":"v:1","detail":"full","body":{"format":"markdown","value":"# Tailored Brands – Gateway Pull Support Guide

Executive Summary

- Gateway Pull retrieves files from Tailored Brands' AWS S3 bucket and delivers them to Appriss Retail ingestion on a fixed schedule.
- Use this guide to quickly check pipelines, agent pool, configuration, S3 source, and housekeeping when troubleshooting.
- Follow the numbered troubleshooting workflow, then review the expanded common issues and escalation/logs sections if the problem persists.

## Overview

Gateway Pull connects to Tailored Brands' AWS S3 bucket, retrieves data files on a scheduled basis, and delivers them to the Appriss Retail ingestion destination. This page explains what to check when investigating issues with the Tailored Brands pull and how to work through common failure scenarios.

## Client Details

| **Field** | **Value** |
| --- | --- |
| **Client Name** | Tailored Brands |
| **Customer ID** | 209 |
| **Source Type** | AWS S3 |
| **S3 Bucket** | `tbawssf01nonprod` |
| **Output Encryption** | No |
| **Output Compression** | No (files arrive pre-compressed as .zip for POS transactions) |
| **File Retention** | 3 days |
| **Production Agent Pool** | `prd-gateway-sh-pool` |

## Azure DevOps Quick Links

| **Resource** | **Link** |
| --- | --- |
| **Pull Pipeline** | [https://dev.azure.com/appriss-si/Appriss%20Retail%20Gateway/\_build?definitionId=117](https://dev.azure.com/appriss-si/Appriss%20Retail%20Gateway/_build?definitionId=117) |
| **Destination Pipeline** | [https://dev.azure.com/appriss-si/Appriss%20Retail%20Gateway/\_build?definitionId=118](https://dev.azure.com/appriss-si/Appriss%20Retail%20Gateway/_build?definitionId=118) |
| **Agent Pool** | [https://dev.azure.com/appriss-si/\_settings/agentqueues](https://dev.azure.com/appriss-si/_settings/agentqueues) |
| **Variable Groups** | [https://dev.azure.com/appriss-si/Appriss%20Retail%20Gateway/\_library](https://dev.azure.com/appriss-si/Appriss%20Retail%20Gateway/_library) |
| **Environments** | [https://dev.azure.com/appriss-si/Appriss%20Retail%20Gateway/\_environments](https://dev.azure.com/appriss-si/Appriss%20Retail%20Gateway/_environments) |

## Pull Schedule

| **Schedule** | **Frequency** | **Branch** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `*/30 * * * *` | Every 30 minutes | `main` |

The pull runs automatically every 30 minutes, continuously, even if no new files are present in the bucket.

## Feeds

Tailored Brands has 11 active feeds, all pulling from the S3 bucket tbawssf01nonprod. POS transactions arrive as .zip files (pre-compressed by the client); all other feeds are plain .txt.

| **Feed Name** | **S3 Path** | **File Extension** | **Notes** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| postransactions | `vendors/appriss/outbound/Tlogs/` | `.zip` | Pre-compressed by client |
| coupon | `vendors/appriss/outbound/Coupon/` | `.txt` |  |
| customer | `vendors/appriss/outbound/Customer/` | `.txt` |  |
| humanresources | `vendors/appriss/outbound/Human_Resource/` | `.txt` |  |
| item | `vendors/appriss/outbound/Item/` | `.txt` |  |
| loyalty | `vendors/appriss/outbound/Loyalty/` | `.txt` |  |
| overshorts | `vendors/appriss/outbound/Over_shorts/` | `.txt` |  |
| promotion | `vendors/appriss/outbound/Promotion/` | `.txt` |  |
| rental | `vendors/appriss/outbound/Rental/` | `.txt` |  |
| store | `vendors/appriss/outbound/Store/` | `.txt` |  |

## Azure DevOps Pipelines

| **Pipeline** | **File** | **Purpose** | **What to Check** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Pull Pipeline** | `gateway.pull.tailoredbrands.shpool.yaml` | Connects to S3, downloads files | Failed runs, AWS authentication errors, S3 access issues |
| **Destination Pipeline** | `destination.tailoredbrands.pipeline.yaml` | Sends processed files to Appriss ingestion | Failed runs, delivery errors, lock conflicts |

## Troubleshooting Workflow

Use this ordered workflow to investigate issues with the Tailored Brands Gateway Pull:

1. Check Azure DevOps – Pull Pipeline
    - Confirm the pipeline gateway.pull.tailoredbrands.shpool.yaml is triggering on schedule and review the most recent runs.
    - Verify the environment gateway-pull-main and variable group gateway\_pull\_main\_vars are correctly referenced.
    - Look for AWS authentication errors such as AccessDenied or InvalidClientTokenId and S3 connectivity issues in the logs.
2. Check Azure DevOps – Destination Pipeline
    - Review recent runs of destination.tailoredbrands.pipeline.yaml for failures or long-running jobs.
    - Confirm the environment gateway-pull-main and variable groups gateway\_pull\_main\_vars and gateway\_pull\_tailoredbrands\_destination\_main are in use.
    - Check for failed file delivery, SFTP connection errors, or lock-related conflicts.
3. Validate Azure Agent Pool
    - Open the prd-gateway-sh-pool and ensure there are healthy online agents available.
    - Check for a large queue backlog or jobs stuck in running state from previous executions.
4. Confirm Azure Storage – Settings File
    - Navigate to the artefacts container in Azure Storage.
    - Verify the settings file exists at /rtiaas/solutions/gateway/pull/customers/tailoredbrands/tailoredbrands.pull.settings.json.
    - Check that the file content is valid and not corrupted; if missing or malformed, the pull will fail to start.
5. Review Azure Storage – Distributed Locks
    - Inspect the lock storage (Azure Table Storage) for entries related to Tailored Brands.
    - Identify any locks older than 60 minutes that have not been cleaned by housekeeping, which may indicate a crashed run.
6. Verify Source – AWS S3 Bucket
    - Confirm that the tbawssf01nonprod bucket is reachable with the configured AWS access key and secret key (stored in variable groups).
    - Check IAM permissions for read access to the relevant S3 paths for each feed.
    - Ensure files are present in the expected S3 paths and that filenames and extensions match the feed expectations.
7. Check Housekeeping Pipeline
    - Review runs of housekeeping.pipeline.shpool.yaml, which executes every 30 minutes to clean up old files and stale locks.
    - Look for recent failures that might leave stale data, checkpoints, or lock entries that interfere with normal processing.

## Services to Check (Reference)

The sections below summarise each service involved in the Tailored Brands pull and the key checks to perform.

### 1. Azure DevOps – Pull Pipeline

Pipeline: gateway.pull.tailoredbrands.shpool.yaml

Environment: gateway-pull-main

Variable Group: gateway\_pull\_main\_vars

Check for:

- Recent run failures or runs not triggering on the expected schedule.
- AWS authentication errors (AccessDenied, InvalidClientTokenId).
- S3 connectivity or permission issues indicated in logs.

### 2. Azure DevOps – Destination Pipeline

Pipeline: destination.tailoredbrands.pipeline.yaml

Environment: gateway-pull-main

Variable Groups: gateway\_pull\_main\_vars, gateway\_pull\_tailoredbrands\_destination\_main

Check for:

- Failed file delivery or retries in logs.
- SFTP connection errors when sending to ingestion.
- Lock conflicts preventing processing or delivery.

### 3. Azure Agent Pool

Pool: prd-gateway-sh-pool

Check for:

- Agents offline or disabled that could block queued jobs.
- Queue backlog indicating insufficient capacity or hung jobs.
- Agents stuck on a previous run for this customer.

### 4. Azure Storage – Settings File

Container: artefacts

Path: /rtiaas/solutions/gateway/pull/customers/tailoredbrands/tailoredbrands.pull.settings.json

Check for:

- Presence of the tailoredbrands.pull.settings.json file at the specified path.
- Intact and valid configuration content (no truncation or corruption).
- Awareness that if this file is missing or corrupted, the pull will fail to start.

### 5. Azure Storage – Distributed Locks

Check for:

- Lock entries associated with Tailored Brands feeds that remain after runs complete.
- Stale locks older than 60 minutes that may indicate a pipeline crash mid-run.

### 6. Source – AWS S3 Bucket

Bucket: tbawssf01nonprod

Authentication: AWS access key and secret key (stored in variable groups)

Check for:

- General bucket accessibility from the pipeline using the configured credentials.
- IAM permission errors or policy changes that might block access.
- Files present in the expected S3 paths for each feed with the correct extensions.

### 7. Housekeeping Pipeline

Pipeline: housekeeping.pipeline.shpool.yaml

This pipeline runs every 30 minutes to clean up old files and stale locks.

Check for:

- Recent housekeeping failures that leave stale data in storage.
- Uncleared lock entries that could block new runs.

## Common Issues and Step-by-Step Checks

| **Symptom** | **Likely Cause** | **Where to Look** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No files arriving at destination | Pull pipeline not running or S3 bucket empty | Azure DevOps – Pull Pipeline runs; S3 bucket paths |
| Files pulled but not delivered | Destination pipeline failing | Azure DevOps – Destination Pipeline runs |
| AWS AccessDenied error | IAM credentials expired or permissions changed | AWS IAM, variable group gateway\_pull\_main\_vars |
| Pipeline stuck / not completing | Stale lock or agent offline | Azure Table Storage locks, Agent Pool status |
| .zip files not processing | POS transactions arrive pre-zipped — this is expected | Confirm postransactions feed expects .zip |
| Settings file error on startup | Config missing or malformed | Artefacts container, tailoredbrands.pull.settings.json |
| Files being re-processed | Checkpoint/lock cleanup issue | Housekeeping pipeline, Azure Table Storage |

### Detailed Checks by Symptom

#### No files arriving at destination

1. Confirm recent runs of gateway.pull.tailoredbrands.shpool.yaml and ensure they are succeeding.
2. Review logs for S3 listing and download steps to confirm whether any files are found.
3. Check S3 paths for each feed to verify files are present and new since the last successful run.

#### Files pulled but not delivered

1. Verify that destination.tailoredbrands.pipeline.yaml is triggering after successful pulls.
2. Inspect destination pipeline logs for delivery or SFTP-related errors.
3. Look for lock conflicts or retries that might delay or block delivery.

#### AWS AccessDenied or authentication errors

1. Check variable group gateway\_pull\_main\_vars for the configured AWS access key and secret key values.
2. Validate IAM policies for the associated user or role to ensure read access to tbawssf01nonprod and the feed paths.
3. Re-run the pull pipeline and confirm that errors such as AccessDenied or InvalidClientTokenId are resolved.

#### Pipeline stuck or not completing

1. Check the prd-gateway-sh-pool for agents that appear stuck or offline running Tailored Brands jobs.
2. Inspect distributed lock entries in Azure Table Storage for locks that are older than 60 minutes and not cleared.
3. Confirm recent runs of housekeeping.pipeline.shpool.yaml to ensure stale locks are being cleaned.

#### .zip files not processing

1. Confirm that the issue relates specifically to the postransactions feed, which uses .zip files.
2. Review configuration to ensure that .zip is the expected extension for postransactions and that no decompression step is incorrectly failing.
3. Validate that other .txt feeds are processing normally to isolate the issue to this feed.

#### Settings file error on startup

1. Navigate to the artefacts container and locate /rtiaas/solutions/gateway/pull/customers/tailoredbrands/tailoredbrands.pull.settings.json.
2. Open the file and confirm it is complete and correctly formatted for the gateway pull configuration.
3. If the file is missing or corrupted, restore the correct version and re-run the pull pipeline.

#### Files being re-processed

1. Check the housekeeping.pipeline.shpool.yaml runs to ensure checkpoint and lock cleanup is occurring every 30 minutes.
2. Inspect Azure Table Storage for duplicate or stale checkpoint and lock entries for the same files.
3. Validate that retention and de-duplication logic in the configuration has not been altered.

## Notes

- Tailored Brands uses AWS S3 as the source — no SFTP is involved on the pull side.
- Customer ID is 209.
- The POS transactions feed (postransactions) delivers .zip files — this is pre-compressed by the client and is expected.
- All other feeds deliver plain .txt files with no additional encryption.
- Processed files are retained for 3 days before housekeeping removes them.
- Stale locks are automatically cleaned up after 60 minutes.

## Escalation & Useful Logs

### When to Escalate

- If both pull and destination pipelines are running successfully but data is still missing or inconsistent.
- If you identify persistent AWS authentication or IAM permission issues that cannot be resolved via configuration updates.
- If housekeeping appears to be functioning but files continue to re-process or locks remain stuck beyond 60 minutes.

### Key Logs and Locations

- Azure DevOps build logs for gateway.pull.tailoredbrands.shpool.yaml to review S3 connection, file discovery, and download activity.
- Azure DevOps build logs for destination.tailoredbrands.pipeline.yaml to inspect delivery, SFTP connection, and ingestion handoff details.
- Azure Storage tables for distributed lock and checkpoint entries tied to Tailored Brands feeds.
- Azure Storage artefacts container for the tailoredbrands.pull.settings.json configuration file and any related metadata required for the pull.

{"data":{"id":"475190689809","type":"page","title":"Setting up SSO","status":"current","spaceId":"1091698695","snapshotToken":"v:5","detail":"full","body":{"format":"markdown","value":"# Overview

Single Sign-On (SSO) is a mechanism that allows users to authenticate to various applications using singular domain account. You might have encountered this when you logged to any service using other service (e.g. logged to Instagram using Google account, logged to Steam using Meta account, logged to Rippling or 15Five using [trebu.co](http://trebu.co) account).

Our customers usually wish to authenticate to secure using their domain accounts. For that to work we have to set up SSO configuration. Customer has to prepare it from their side as well.

Information about user is sent using SSO via document called Assertion. This XML document contains all information about user (personal details, their location, their role) as well as security certificate (X509 certificate)

All information required to set up SSO can be usually found in a XML document provided by customer called “Metadata”.

There are various SSO methods. Most popular one is called SAML. At Appriss Retail we support SAML and OpenID.

Customers can use any SSO provider on their end. Most popular ones are Azure AD (Identity ID{TBD}) and Octa.

There are three additional features (apart from authentication) that are very useful:

- Just In Time provisioning (JIT) – customer do not have to set up accounts prior to users logging in. If system detects a new user logon – their account will be created automatically using information provided via SSO (First Name, Last Name, Email)
- Group/Location/Team mapping from Assertion – we can configure a mapping document that will grab additional information from assertion and apply Permission Groups/Locations/Teams to user in Secure. If that is created – no user maintenance is required
- Group/Location/Team mapping from File – we can set load and transform process in order to apply Permission Groups/Locations/Teams to user in Secure. If that is created – no user maintenance is required

At Appriss we are offering two versions of SSO:

- Base SSO: all customers are getting this option for free with Secure. It allows for minimal setup - authentication only. No Group/Location/Team mappings allowed. These are instead maintained manually by client using SSO+ portal
- Advanced SSO: this paid option adds two possible configurations:
    - Group/Location/Team mapping from assertion
    - Group/Location/Team mapping from File


# Important Notice

**Before setting up SSO please reach out to PM/UC and confirm whether customer should have Base SSO or have they paid for Advanced.**

SSO module is hosted on IIS. Because of that, all changes to SSO require not only Release to be ran, but also App Pool Recycle (we have dedicated Pipeline for that).

SSO configuration has dependencies with various elements of Secure Platform: Permission Groups, Teams, Standard Location Hierarchy, Secure Incident, Engage, Over/Shorts, Cashier Coaching. Whilst setting up Base SSO can be done at any time – even day one of signed contract, Advanced SSO required users to understand Secure a little and depended modules to be created and configured (e.g. If configuring mapping for Secure Incident Security Groups using SSO – Secure Incident site has to be created and customer has to already finish work on Security Groups. You won’t be able to configure the mapping if Security Groups are not yet decided.).

We are setting up SSO to meet customer needs and their operational requirements. Because of that it is crucial to work on SSO with customer, explaining them possibilities, mentioning limitations and results of various scenarios. SSO configuration is usually complex and takes weeks to complete.

When customer has also purchased Secure Incident – they will use Secure as a only logon platform to both Secure and Incident. Because of that you will need to set up Universal SSO between Secure and Incident. Whilst Secure utilizes Permission Groups – Incident has Security Groups and they do not match. Because of this you have to prepare not only mapping to Secure, but also to Incident


# Prerequisites

- Customer Metadata for QA and PROD environment. Its usually sent in a form of a XML file or a link to webpage with XML document.
- If Metadata does not have any information about Assertion Attributes you will need to ask for sample SAML assertion. If this cannot be obtained – after initial configuration you need to ask customer to log in to Secure using SSO and get sample SAML assertion from Secure Logs.
- Meeting with customer Business representative and SSO (IT Infrastructure) representative from customer side to discuss what are customer needs, what they can provide, how we can create it and plan the implementation.
- If customer purchased Secure Incident – Security Groups in Secure Incident have to be established.

 

# Prerequisites for customer

- Appriss Retail metadata (It is sent by PM to customer)
    - sso.SAML2ConsumerURLUniqueID – this is URL given to customer that triggers SSO logon process. Its always CPF.Core.ExternalApplicationAddress + “/sso/saml2”.
    - sso.SAML2UniqueID – this is Unique Identifier given to customer that allows logon to happen. Its always CPF.Core.ExternalApplicationAddress without “/secure” at the end.  
  
You should be always sending 4 values to customer. An example metadata from us would look like:
    - QA Customer URL: [https://wegmans-qa.apprissretailcloud.com/secure/sso/saml](https://wegmans-qa.apprissretailcloud.com/secure/sso/saml2)
    - QA UniqueID: <https://wegmans-qa.apprissretailcloud.com>
    - PROD Customer URL: <https://wegmans.apprissretailcloud.com/secure/sso/saml2>
    - PROD UniqueID: <https://wegmans.apprissretailcloud.com> 
- Meeting with Appriss Retail Product Delivery employee (and preferably PM/UC who understand their business) to discuss and plan configuration


# Metting with Customer

It is crucial to meet with customer before any work is done to understand what is needed and explain what we can provide. Below you can find an example process:

1. PM reaches out to you that SSO needs to be set up. They should schedule a meeting with customer. There should be at least one Business representative (ideally power user of Secure) and one IT resource.
2. Check whether customer will use Base SSO or whether they purchased Advanced SSO
3. Start the meeting with short introduction on what are you trying to accomplish Today. You can follow this message:

> *The aim of having SSO is to automate provisioning and shift Security/User assignment from Secure to your organization. *  
> *We use Just in Time provisioning – meaning all users will have their accounts created automatically upon first logon. You do not need to create anything prior.*  
> *The usual process for SSO Implementation follows these steps:*
> 
> 1. *We will send you our metadata that consists of UniqueID and CustomerURL. It should be already provided by PM in SSO documentation.*
> 2. *You \[customer\] need to provide us Metadata and X509 Certificate in exchange*
> 3. *We will configure SSO on our end*
> 4. *Once its done, we will contact you via email and ask to test SSO by logging to Secure using SSO*
> 5. *In return you need to send us result of the logon process and name of the user who attempted it*
> 6. *We will review logs and check if everything is working as expected.*
> 7. *Once completed, we can push to PROD.*
> 
> *Please bear in mind that this is just authentication part. All Permission Groups, Locations and Teams assignments should be handled manually by any of your users with Administrators Permission Group. They have access to SSO+ portal where these changes can be made. Our SE should have a training session with you on how to use it.*


This is all for the Base SSO. If customer has purchased Advanced SSO you need to continue:

 

> *This was just the authentication part. After its completed, we can start working on Advanced SSO which is automated provisioning of Permission Groups, Teams and Locations.*
> 
> *Lets start with Permission Groups. There are 5 standard Permission Groups in Secure:*
> 
> 1. *Administrators*
> 2. *EBR Analysts*
> 3. *EBR Investigator Supervisors*
> 4. *EBR Investigators*
> 5. *EBR Store Users*


You should check before the meeting which modules customer has purchased. If none – skip this section


> *There are also special groups dedicated to additional modules.*
> 
> 1. *Cashier Coaching Managers*
> 2. *Cashier Coaching Administrators*
> 3. *Verify Users*
> 4. *Verify Elevated Users*
> 5. *Verify Returns Auth User*
> 6. *Verify Override User*
> 7. *Verify Void User*
> 8. *Over Short Analysts*
> 9. *ApprissCase Users*
> 
> *10.   ApprissCase Search Users*
> 
> *11.   Audit Users*
> 
> *You should decide now what Permission Groups you want to use. You need to start sending us a Role attribute in SAML assertion. You also need to prepare a mapping document {TBD – link to document} that will explain how your Roles are mapped to Secure Permission Groups. The name of the attribute does not have to be “role”. It could be “group”, “security detail” – pretty much anything.*
> 
> *In similar manner we can set automatic assignment to Teams. Since Teams are created by you \[customer\] – you can have as many teams as you wish and assign people based on any attribute. Usually the same Role attribute is used for that. We always suggest to create at least one-to-one mapping for Role-\>Teams assignment.*
> 
> *Now lets talk about Locations. If you want to assign users to Location automatically, you need to start sending us Location attribute. Again – the name of the attribute can be anything. There are usually two components of Location assignment:*
> 
> 1. *Store assignment. Usually applied to Store Owners / Store Managers / Franchisee Owners. Assigns users to just one or handful of stores. This is usually fairly simple to configure as long as you can provide the data in SAML assertion from your Active Directory.*
> 2. *Levels above store assignment (Department / Zone / Area / All Company etc.). Usually applied to Corporate / Asset Protection / Loss Prevention. From experience – this one is usually a little tricky since Active Directory rarely has correct information. If you are able to provide this in SAML assertion we can grant it to users automatically. Most common is access to All Company for Corporate users.*


If customer has purchased Secure Incident as well as Advanced SSO you need to add this part


> *In similar fashion we can automate assignment for Secure Incident Security Groups. We can map the values from Role attribute to Security Groups. You would need to add this to the mapping document.*
> 
> *What if you do not have required information in Active Directory but you have it somewhere else e.g. HR system feed or spreadsheet and wish to use that instead? We can also set up File Ingestion and Transformation that will automatically feed SSO+ tables. We are more flexible in that scenario and can alter the data as needed, add IF THEN scenarios etc. We can also combine provisioning from SAML assertion and File e.g. grant Permission Groups based on Role attribute from Assertion, but the Location assignment will be based on the File from Workday.*
> 
> *If you wish to use such solution you will have to set up regular (ideally daily) upload of the file to our SFTP endpoint and explain how to use the information/how to map the data.*
> 
> *Once all information is provided to Appriss Retail and required elements are added to SAML Assertion – we can follow the same steps as previously: configure -\> test -\> review tests -\> promote to PROD.*


When you run the meeting like that, the customer should have all required information to decide upon solution architecture. If they have any additional questions you can check FAQ section below.

# FAQ:

1. Q: What providers do we support?  
A: Azure AD {TBD} and OpenID
2. Q: Do you have any requirements for the Attributes?  
A: No. You can use any attribute name you want. In our code we can map data by attribute name.
3. Q: What is the SSO link?  
A: It’s CPF.Core.ExternalApplicationAddress + “/sso/saml2”
4. Q: Do we need to create users in Secure before they log in using SSO?  
A: No. We have JIT therefore all accounts are created automatically upon first logon
5. Q: I already have users in Application using Application logon method type (username+password). What will happen when we switch to SSO?  
A: If email address in SAML Assertion will match email address in already created account – user will log in to their account and the account will be transformed to SSO one.  
If email address in SAML Assertion will not match email address in already created account – user will get new account.  
We can prevent that by updating email addresses in \[C{123}\_{ABC}\_Platform\].\[membership\].\[Users\] before SSO Go Live. You can send the list of all created accounts and ask for customer IT team to verify if email address matches the one they have in Active Directory. This is usually done if SSO is introduced way after Go Live. When sending the file make sure you are sending either encrypted file or at least password protected spreadsheet and provide password with different method of communication.  
If SSO user gets new account we can also fix that. Run queries below to update old account with new email and new account with dummy email  

```
-- GET NEW EMAIL ADDRESS. COPY THE VALUE!
SELECT FirstName, LastName, Email, LastLoginDate 
FROM [C{123}_{ABC}_Platform].[membership].[Users]
WHERE Email like '%{USE TO FIND NEW EMAIL ADDRESS}%'

-- UPDATE NEW ACCOUNT TO DUMMY ONE
UPDATE [C{123}_{ABC}_Platform].[membership].[Users]
SET Email = 'deprecated@clientdomain.com'
, Deleted =  1
, Disabled = 1
, FirstName = 'Deprecated'
, LastName = 'Deprecated'
WHERE Email = '{NEW EMAIL ADDRESS}'

-- UPDATE OLD ACCOUNT TO NEW EMAL
UPDATE [C{123}_{ABC}_Platform].[membership].[Users]
SET Email = '{NEW EMAIL ADDRESS}'
WHERE Email = '{OLD EMAIL ADDRESS}'
```

1. Q: Can one user switch between SSO and Application logon method type as they wish?  
A: No. Once they log in using SSO, they cannot log in again using username and password. If there is a need to go back to Application logon method – A Delivery Consultant or Support employee from Appriss Retail has to update given users account in database. Its only allowed before SSO Go Live – during testing phase in QA/PROD.  

```
UPDATE [C{123}_{ABC}_Platform].[membership].[Users]
SET [AccountType] = 'Normal'
WHERE UserName = '{PASTE USERNAME HERE}'
```
2. Q: Can we use SSO and Application logon method type at the same time?  
A: Preferred answer is no. Customer should use only one or the another. The reason is that its really hard from support perspective and it creates a confusion from customer side.  
However – only for critical situations, that is possible. In Secure LogonMethodType will be set as “Application” and SSO will work anyway. Users have to be warned that once they use SSO, they cannot go back to Application account.
3. Q: Can we use two providers or two separate SSO configurations? E.g. we use one SSO for our corporate users, and separate one for Franchisees.  
A: No, only one SSO configuration is allowed.
4. Q: We do not have purchased Advanced SSO. How we should manage users in Secure?  
A: Any user with Administrators Permission Group have access to SSO+ portal. You can manager user Permission Groups, Teams and Locations from there.
5. Q: We do not have purchased Advanced SSO. There will be thousands of users (corp users + store managers). We do not want to manually add those to SSO+. Is there any option?  
A: Yes. We can offer a one time upload to SSO+ portal through backend. Send this file to User {TBD}, and then prepare INSERT file {TBD} and execute it on PROD at required date. From then on all changes have to be done manually by customer in SSO+
6. Q: What locations can you map?  
A: We can map either individual stores, groups of stores and higher location levels – up to All Company.
7. Q: Do you support lists with separators?  
A: Yes, we support lists. We can work with any separator.
8. Q: Can you grant all users Permission Group by default?  
A: Yes. We support granting specific Permission Groups (and only Permission Groups) by default.
9. Q: We have Advanced SSO with Location Mapping. What happens when Store Manager changes locations?  
A: Their Location in Secure will be updated upon next logon automatically – assuming this information was updated in your Active Directory
10. Q: I have applied additional elements to user in SSO+. But I do not see any results in Users app.   
A: SSO+ is a supplementary information for logon process. User will be updated upon next logon.
11. Q: We have Advanced SSO with Permission Groups mapping. What happens if someone tries to log in without any valid Role?  
A: They can log in with no access or their logon can be denied. Its up to the customer how this should work. Check Configuration Item “SSO.DenyAccessIfNoGroupsMapped”
12. Q: What mapping of Permission Groups and Teams do you support?  
A: Many-to-many. One Role can be mapped to Many Permission Groups/Teams and Many Roles can be mapped to the same Permission Group/Team
13. Q: Do you support conditional mapping? We want to grant users Administrators Permission Group only if they have role “HeadOffice” and email ends like ‘%[Corp.com](http://Corp.com)’  
A: We do not support complex conditions. We do support only simple conditions for location mappings:  
IF \<attribute\> EXISTS AND HAS VALUE \<value\> THEN GRANT \<locationID\> ON LEVEL \<locationlevel\>
14. Q: We store our Departments as descriptions rather than integers. Do you support text assignments?  
A: Yes, we do support assignment to location with both location number and location description.
15. Q: We store our Stores with prefix ST and leading zeros e.g. “ST0488”. Will you be able to work with this?  
A: Yes. We support Regular Expressions to handle such situations.
16. Q: Do SSO Certificates expire?  
A: They do not expire on our end. If your organization has expiration date for Certificate – please send us new one at least three weeks before old one expires.


# Steps

You always start with Base SSO. If customer has purchased Advanced SSO – you should start working on it once Base SSO implementation is completed.

Start with QA configuration:

1. Open QA Metadata file from customer. In there you need to localize three elements:
    1. Provider URL. Its usually located at the end. Look for “HTTP-POST” text
    2. X509 Certificate. There can be multiple X509Certificate nodes, but they all have the same value
    3. Attributes. Look for “ClaimType” text. This unfortunately is often missing from client metadata. If that is the case – go to step {TBD}
2. Navigate to {123}/seed/secure\_ConfigurationItem.json file. In the file add these Configuration Items:
    1. sso.AccessDeniedUrl – should be the same as CPF.Core.ExternalApplicationAddress, but if customer has dedicated one – use theirs
    2. sso.DefaultProviderUrl - CPF.Core.ExternalApplicationAddress  + “sso/saml2”
    3. sso.SAML2ConsumerURL – the same as sso.DefaultProviderUrl
    4. sso.SAML2UniqueID - CPF.Core.ExternalApplicationAddress without “/secure”
    5. sso.SAML2ProdiverURL – value from step 1 a
    6. sso.samlCertificate – take a value from step 1 b. You need to make it json compliant. You can run query below in any Microsoft SQL Database to get the value:  
SELECT TOP 1 ‘{PASTE YOUR CERTIFICATE HERE}’ as Cert  
FROM sys.tables as t1 FOR JSON AUTO – click on result row. Then copy value between double quotation marks.  
Paste it to sso.samlCertificate value
    7. CPF.Core.LogonMethodType – this Configuration Item has one of two values: “sso” and “application”. The former will just have “Sign in” button in logon page that triggers SSO process. The latter has “username and password” logon page. It might be tempting to switch to SSO right away but that is not a good option since users often work in QA whilst SSO being still in configuration/testing (not completed). My suggestion is that you change that Configuration Item value to “sso” in QA and PROD during SSO Go Live. You have to inform customer that from that moment only SSO logon will be available.
    8. sso.SAML2RelayStateEnabled - False
    9. Sso.DenyAccessIfNoGroupsMapped – Set to False initially. For Base SSO you never change it. For Advanced SSO - ask customer what they wish to do with logons that do not have any required group. If they wish to allow users to log in with no access – leave as False. If they wish to deny logon – set to True.  
You should start with False because at first you are always configuring Base SSO therefore no groups are always provided. You can flip this once Permission Groups mapping is added and tested.
    10. Sso.Plus.MapLocationsByCode – False
3. Navigate to {123}/system/sso/saml2configuration.sso (if file doesn’t exist – copy it from Platform). Update these keys:
    1. client-id
    2. client-id-hash
    3. mandatory-claims
    4. iana-timezone

    13. role-mappings

        6. conditional-value

# Error handling

1. User is not authorized to access app – this is on customer side. They need to add users to App in AD
2. Cryptographic error – your certificate is not formatted correctly
3. Customer lands on logon page – either certificate is wrong or mandatory claims are missing or customer has provided no roles/different roles that we have configured and DenyAccessIfNoGroupsMapped is set to True
4. Customer sees one thing in SSO+ and different in Users app

## 2. Problem Statement

Client requests manual insertion of two non-merchandise locations — Store 3710 (Terrain Cafe - Wayland) and Store 3711 (Terrain Osteria - Wayland, per ticket) — into the SSO+/Portal Location Hierarchy under Urban Outfitters \> NON MERCHANDISE (NA) \> VETRI FAMILY (NA), and that they be protected from being purged/overwritten by daily automated location feed updates. These locations are not visible when assigning them to user accounts in SSO+.

## 3. Client Profile

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Client ID | c044\_urb |
| Region | US |
| ARDM Version | V2 (snowtimeV2) |
| Snowflake Schema | ARDM\_PRODUCTION.C044\_URB / C044\_URB\_SNOWTIME |
| Active Systems | SnowTime pipeline, Secure Platform (SSO+), Incident (legacy) |

## 4. Investigation

### 4.1 place.Location by StoreNumber + brand filter (Secure/Platform DB)

**FAIL.** 0 rows returned.

### 4.2 place.Location by StoreNumber only, no filter

**FAIL.** 0 rows — confirms absence, rules out a filter/formatting mismatch.

### 4.3 incident.Store (Platform DB)

**FAIL.** 0 rows for the two stores; a later COUNT(\*) returned only 1 row total for this tenant — table not populated, not the real store source for this client.

### 4.4 Legacy Incident database — Store/LPUser

**POINT OF FAILURE FOUND (positive match, wrong system).** 2 active rows found (Inactive=0), District/Region/Division = 560-VETRI FAMILY (NA) — confirms these are two independent systems: legacy Incident has the stores, Platform/Secure (SSO+) does not.

### 4.5 place.Location sibling lookup (LocationID=3709)

**PASS.** Confirmed the join key is `LocationID = numeric store number` (StoreNumber column is NULL for this client, a `StoreNumber='3709'` lookup returned 0 rows). Returned full hierarchy template: URB/Urban Outfitters → 100099/NON MERCHANDISE (NA) → 100099/NON MERCHANDISE (NA) → 100056/VETRI FAMILY (NA) → NA560/VETRI FAMILY (NA).

### 4.6 REFERENCE\_LOCATION schema + sibling row (Snowflake, MCP snowflake-us)

**PASS.** Confirmed `place.Location` is fed from Snowflake's `REFERENCE_LOCATION` via `PLACE_SPOTLIGHTSEARCHLOCATIONFEED` — an incremental watermark-based upsert that never deletes rows (`ShouldRemove` always FALSE). A manual insert will not be purged by subsequent feed syncs.

### 4.7 Code review — ManageStores.aspx.vb + MigrateToLocationFromStore

**FINDING.** "Manage Stores" (legacy Incident) and "Location Hierarchies" (Platform/SSO+) are independent, unsynced systems. A bridging procedure (`incident.MigrateToLocationFromStore`) exists but requires `incident.Store` to be populated — which it is not for this tenant (see 4.3). Not usable here.

## 5. Root Cause Statement

| Field | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| What broke | Stores 3710/3711 (non-merchandise event/cafe sites) are invisible in Secure/Platform's Location Hierarchy (SSO+) and cannot be assigned to user accounts |
| Why | These sites are structurally excluded from Urban Outfitters' automated POS location feed (non-transactional) → never populate Snowflake's REFERENCE\_LOCATION → never sync to `place.Location` |
| Scope | 2 locations, Urban Outfitters (c044\_urb), VETRI FAMILY (NA) hierarchy branch |
| Business impact | Store staff cannot get SSO+ access to these active, open locations — blocks incident logging |
| Evidence | 0 rows in `place.Location` for these 2 locations (verified twice); 2 confirmed active rows in the separate legacy Incident system; sibling LocationID 3709 confirms expected hierarchy shape; `PLACE_SPOTLIGHTSEARCHLOCATIONFEED` source confirms upsert-only (no-purge) sync |

## 6. Additional Findings

- Internal note (Ryan Barlow, 2026-09-15) recommended requiring the client to add these via their automated feed. Technically consistent with root cause, but the ticket description states these sites are excluded from the standard feed by design, and 2023 precedent (RCS-8044/DO-514, same client/hierarchy) shows this exact category of site (a restaurant, store 3701) was permanently absent from the feed. A feed-only fix may leave the client blocked indefinitely.
- Store 3711's name per ticket ("Terrain Osteria - Wayland") does not match the confirmed legacy Incident system name ("Terrain Events - Wayland") — needs confirmation before the insert.

## 7. Recommended Fix

### Option A — Manual INSERT into REFERENCE\_LOCATION (Recommended)

Insert the two locations directly into `ARDM_PRODUCTION.C044_URB.REFERENCE_LOCATION` (Snowflake), copying hierarchy structure from sibling LocationID 3709 and confirmed data from the legacy Incident Store table. Tag `FILENAME='MANUAL-RCS-28909'` for traceability/reversibility. Upsert-only sync means no purge risk; if the client's feed ever delivers these locations, the next build will correctly update the row. Low risk, fully reversible via a DELETE on the FILENAME marker. **Confirm Store 3711's real name (Events vs Osteria) before running.**

Ask client to add these two non-merchandise sites to their location feed export, mirroring existing Terrain Cafe/Osteria sites' hierarchy. Lower long-term operational cost but leaves client blocked meanwhile; 2023 precedent suggests this category of site may never make it into the feed.
